newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian winter food grain sowings down 9.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russian winter food grain sowings down 9.5 pct.

text.p: Russia, on the heels of its second bad harvest in a row, has sown only 13.0 million hectares to winter food grains for harvesting in 1997, a 9.5 percent drop on last year's level, official data showed on Monday.
Figures from the State Statistics Committee put winter wheat, rye, barley and rice sowings at 13.0 million hectares, below the 14.2 million sown in late 1995 for harvesting in 1996.
Winter feed grains were sown to 0.8 million hectares for harvesting in 1997, below the 1.1 million year-ago level.
Farmers completed sowing in 1996, but the committee only recently finished compiling its data.
A committee spokeswoman said there was no breakdown for individual grains.
Winter wheat comprises up to 50 percent of total sowings in the grain-belt Northern Caucasus, but less in other regions.
Russia's net grain harvest in 1996 -- the country does not use the crop marketing-year calendar system -- was a woeful 69.0 million tonnes, after 63.4 million in 1995.
